newsitem.title: FRANCE: Spain, France propose Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: Spain, France propose Zaire force.

text.p: France and Spain want the idea of a multi-national force to be considered in order to guarantee distribution of humanitarian aid to refugees in Zaire, Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Monday.

Earlier, French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette called on the United States, European and African countries to hold urgent talks on restoring security in eastern Zaire and averting disaster for more than a million refugees fleeing fighting.
De Charette did not specifically mention troops.

Matutes, speaking at a Franco-Spanish summit in the Mediterranean port of Marseille, said the two were ready to consider a military force, adding the two European allies hoped for help from the United States, presumably for air transport.
Matutes said both Rwanda and Zaire would have to agree not to place obstacles in the way of distributing humanitarian aid.
"If these conditions exist, France and Spain are in favour of considering the creation of this force, for which the collaboration of the United States will also be very important," he told reporters.
"Then we would have the minimum security conditions for this force to proceed with the distribution of humanitarian aid," he added.
In Bonn, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel called for a special meeting of the U.N. Security Council on the crisis in Zaire. U.N. sources said the meeting was likely on Tuesday.
Tutsi rebels announced a three-week ceasefire in eastern Zaire on Monday after a lightning two-week offensive.
The French military says mounting a humanitarian operation to save refugees in eastern Zaire is feasible, but Paris first wants a clear international mandate.
Matutes said creating the force would need the support of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.

"We single-handedly and successfully carried out a similar operation in Rwanda in 1994 to end ethnic killings and allow aid to be brought to populations in danger of starvation and epidemic," a senior French officer told Reuters on Monday.

Most aid agencies have pulled out of east Zaire, where they were helping about a million mostly Rwandan Hutu refugees trapped by fighting between the Zairean army and ethnic Tutsi rebels backed by the Tutsi-led Rwandan army.

Officials said the French government was waiting to see whether African heads of state, due to discuss the Zaire fighting at a meeting in Nairobi on Tuesday, would call for action by the European Union.
France is still smarting from charges from African countries and some of its own European allies that its Rwanda intervention was mostly aimed at advancing French policy objectives.
De Charette said a possible international operation would only be temporary and would allow refugees to return to their camps and villagers to return home.

The French officer who described details of the possible operation said that, as in Rwanda two years ago, a Zaire operation would probably aim to set up "safe haven" areas where refugees could safely gather for food and medical treatment.
Problems could come from the Zairean regular army, whose forces in the area he dismissed as without military value, or from Hutu militias or Tutsi forces.

"In Rwanda, we had no more than 2,500 men on the ground and that was sufficient to discourage anyone from stealing food from refugees. I don't foresee any problems as long as we are strong and look strong," he said.
France already has troops based in several African locations and can also draw on professional paratroop, Foreign Legion and Marine units based in France and used to operating in Africa.
